messages.subject: Trap covariates + rsfDF covariates?
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

I'm working with a remote camera dataset that has accompanying telemetry data. Right now the models I'm running are set to RSF = F, but I'm interested in adding covariates to an rsfDF. However, I'm wondering is it possible to run models with spatial covariates on the trap locations that cannot also be included in the rsfDF? For example trap covariates like remote camera model used, or the recreation level on the trail where the camera was set - things that matter for traps but aren't applicable to the full rsfDF. In the few tests I've done these kinds of models don't work, I'm not sure if I'm attempting something that isn't correct/possible or maybe coding something incorrectly.

Thank you!
Greta

messages.subject: Trouble fitting model with spatial covariate - "dims do not match length of object"
messages.subject_clean: Trouble fitting model with spatial covariate - "dims do not match length of object"
messages.body_plain:
Hi, I’m fairly new to oSCR and trying to get a multi-session model up and running but have encountered a problem when I try to fit the model using a continuous spatial covariate on density. I extracted values from a raster using the updated function extract.rast2() that Chris Sutherland defined in another post(https://groups.google.com/u/0/g/oscr_package/c/EA1rFC4OWH0/m/9IMysJUuAwAJ) as follows:

extract.rast2 <- function(ss, rast, mult = 1, cov.name <http://cov.name> = "val.1",

                          buffer=NULL, method="simple", fun = mean){

  for(i in 1:length(ss)){

    tmpS <- ss[[i]][, c("X", "Y")] * mult

    r1 <- raster::extract(rast, tmpS, buffer=buffer, fun = fun, na.rm=T)

    ss[[i]][, cov.name <http://cov.name>] <- r1

  }

  return(ss)

}

# extract values of raster for use as state-space covariates and append to ssDF

ss_covs2 <- extract.rast2(ss = ss_test1,

                         rast = imperv,

                         mult = 1,

                         cov.name <http://cov.name> = "imperv",

                         buffer = NULL,

                         method = "simple",

                         fun = mean)

This % impervious surface raster encompasses all state-space points, and everything looks fine when I plot it for each session with trap coordinates overlaid. However, I get the following error message when I try to fit any model that uses D ~ impervious:

m02a <- oSCR.fit(model = list(D ~ imperv, p0 ~ 1, sig ~ 1), sf_cat, ss_covs2, trimS = 900)

# Error in f(x, ...) :

# dims [product 766] do not match the length of object [809]

Any idea what the issue might be? The odd thing is that the model fits when I use the same function to extract values from a different continuous raster (% canopy) for the ssDF and use that as a covariate on D instead. (These two layers are moderately correlated and I’d prefer to use the impervious surface one because it’s more up-to-date.)

Thank you in advance, and thanks for all the helpful posts in this group!

messages.subject: error in data2oscr fixed (potential effect on previous analyses... )
messages.subject_clean: error in data2oscr fixed (potential effect on previous analyses... )
messages.body_plain:
hi all,

I encountered an error in data2oscr today in which, internally, when the EDF file is sorted by individual ID it might be the case that the sex variable was not similarly sorted. Its therefore possible that sex information was scrambled and this would obviously affect any models that were run that included sex on either p0 or sigma.

 I'm fairly certain that this may only have affected analyses in which remove.zeros = FALSE. This is a somewhat obscure feature of data2oscr which produces the "full 3-d encounter history array" for the multi-session data set.  That is, it preserves the individual ID across sessions so that if individual Bob259 is in y3d[29,,] for session 1 then it will also be in y3d[29,,] for session 2.  In this case, only people who wanted the 3-d encounter history to run open models in JAGS or similar could have wound up with an error. Possibly this is a small group of people.

  You should re-install oSCR from github.

regards
andy
